role.altitude: The brokerage clerk keeps judging flagged cases, checking forms before they go out, chasing failed transfers and deciding on margin calls with the credit officer; typing forms, matching instructions, downloading prices and recomputing margins by hand shrink.
skills_to_grow: Handling the exceptions that rules flag, and keeping those rules current
role.ambitious_version: A clerk who sees every collateral shortfall the morning it appears and spends the day on the cases that need judgement.

tasks.short: Receive transaction requests from stockholders, check them against holder records, prepare forms such as receipts, withdrawal orders, transmittal papers or transfer confirmations, check the final forms, send the confirmation and file them.

steps.what: Stockholder submits the transaction request in the online form
Brokerage clerk checks the request against the holder's identity and holdings
Brokerage clerk prepares forms such as receipts, withdrawal orders, transmittal papers or transfer confirmations
Brokerage clerk checks the final forms
Brokerage clerk sends the approved confirmation to the stockholder
Brokerage clerk files the forms with the transaction

approvals.approved_version: the confirmation as checked by the clerk in s4; any change needs a new check

tasks.design: Stockholders submit requests in a structured online form with their account number. Fixed rules match the request to the holder record and holdings and flag mismatches. Forms are generated from the request and the record instead of typed. The clerk checks every final form, sends the confirmation and the forms are stored with the transaction. Paper requests are still typed.
tasks.previous_blocker: Each form was typed from a letter or call.
tasks.enabler_now: Online request forms linked to holder records and form templates.
tasks.still_hard: Requests from heirs or companies with unusual paperwork.
tasks.human_edge: Spotting a request that does not fit the holder's pattern.

reach.learn: Whether online requests are complete more often.

evidence.claim: A document capture product checks orders against customer, stock and price rules and routes exceptions to people.
Self-service forms and integrations write once into the records app.

assumptions: Boundary: from request to filed forms; settlement is a separate task.
Input contract for s3: requests from the online form (filled by stockholders in s1, about 70%) and holder records in the securities system; paper requests are typed; s3 is priced at that share.
Stockholders' effort on the form is about what a letter took and sits in s1.
Checking and sending keep their full time.
unknowns: Share of stockholders who use the online form.

already_counted.description: Brokerage clerk handles mismatches the rules flag.

incremental.description: Brokerage clerk keeps form templates current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many paper requests from older holders; high: mostly online requests.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Receive transfer instructions, match them with counterparties and schedule settlement, have the release approved, release instructions, schedule and coordinate transfer and delivery of remaining paper security certificates, chase failed transfers and record completed transfers.

steps.what: Brokerage clerk receives transfer instructions from companies, departments and customers
Brokerage clerk matches instructions with counterparties and schedules settlement dates
Operations supervisor approves the final settlement instructions
Brokerage clerk releases the approved instructions to the depository
Brokerage clerk schedules courier delivery of remaining paper security certificates
Brokerage clerk chases failed or late transfers with counterparties
Brokerage clerk records completed transfers

approvals.approved_version: the settlement instructions as approved by the operations supervisor in s3; any change goes back for approval

tasks.design: Instructions from custodians and counterparties arrive as standard settlement messages into the securities system instead of mail, and fixed rules match them on security, quantity, date and counterparty, leaving unmatched items for the clerk. The supervisor approves before the clerk releases them to the depository. Settlement status comes back from the depository and updates the transfer record. Paper certificates and failed transfers are still handled by people.
tasks.previous_blocker: Instructions were matched by hand in spreadsheets from mails and faxes.
tasks.enabler_now: Standard settlement messages and automatic matching in securities systems.
tasks.still_hard: Counterparties that keep failing to deliver.
tasks.human_edge: Getting a failing counterparty to settle today.

evidence.claim: Matching records on fixed fields is deterministic; spreadsheet trackers are the glue today.

assumptions: Boundary: from instruction to recorded transfer; trading is outside.
Input contract for s1 and s2: standard settlement messages sent by custodians and counterparties, about 80% of instructions; others arrive by mail and are keyed; s1 and s2 are priced at that share.
Input contract for s7: settlement status messages from the depository.
Approving, releasing, courier work and chasing keep their full time; the supervisor's time is outside the clerk's savings.
unknowns: Share of paper certificates still held.

incremental.description: Brokerage clerk keeps counterparty standing data current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many paper certificates and mailed instructions; high: mostly book-entry transfers with standard messages.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Load daily stock prices, compute fluctuations and collateral values, judge which accounts need additional collateral to secure loans, prepare margin call notices, have them approved and send them.

steps.what: Brokerage clerk gets daily stock prices for the pledged securities
Brokerage clerk computes fluctuations, collateral values and margins per loan
Brokerage clerk judges which accounts need additional collateral
Brokerage clerk prepares margin call notices
Credit officer approves the final margin call notices
Brokerage clerk sends the approved margin call notices to clients

approvals.approved_version: the margin call notices as approved by the credit officer in s5; any change goes back for approval

tasks.design: Closing prices load each morning from the market data feed into the collateral system, which computes collateral value, haircut and margin per loan from the loan records and lists accounts below their threshold. The clerk judges which accounts need a call, with knowledge of the client and the security. Notices are filled from a template with the computed figures, the credit officer approves and the clerk sends. No call is made by the system alone.
tasks.previous_blocker: Prices were downloaded and margins recomputed in spreadsheets each day.
tasks.enabler_now: Market data feeds into collateral systems with fixed margin formulas.
tasks.still_hard: Thinly traded securities with unreliable prices.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing when a dip is noise and when a client is in trouble.
tasks.altitude: Less computing; judgement on calls stays.

reach.learn: Whether shortfalls are caught a day earlier.

evidence.claim: Computations such as interest and fares are plain code; margin formulas are the same kind.
No solely automated decision with legal effect without a legal basis; the clerk and credit officer decide on calls.

assumptions: Boundary: from daily prices to margin call notices sent; collection of collateral is outside.
Input contract for s1: closing prices from the market data vendor's feed for listed securities, about 90% of pledged positions; others are priced by hand; s1 is priced at that share.
Input contract for s2: loans and pledged holdings recorded by loan administration in the collateral system; haircuts set by the credit officer.
Judging and sending keep their full time; the credit officer's time is outside the clerk's savings.

already_counted.description: Brokerage clerk checks prices the feed marks as stale or missing.

incremental.description: Brokerage clerk keeps haircut and threshold tables current with the credit officer.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many unlisted or illiquid securities priced by hand; high: mostly listed securities on the feed.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Pull ownership and transaction records, verify ownership and transaction information and dividend distribution instructions against tax and sanction rules using stock records and reports, judge flagged cases and record the verification.

steps.what: Brokerage clerk pulls ownership and transaction records from the stock records
Brokerage clerk verifies ownership, tax status and dividend distribution instructions against the rules
Brokerage clerk judges flagged cases and decides what is needed
Brokerage clerk records the verification results

tasks.design: The holder list for a dividend run comes straight from the securities system instead of exported spreadsheets. Fixed rules check each holder's tax status, residence and withholding rate against the tax forms on file, check names against the sanction list, and check payment instructions against bank details, flagging anything missing or odd. The clerk judges flagged cases. Results are recorded per holder in the system with the rule outcome.
tasks.previous_blocker: Ownership and tax data were checked by hand from exports.
tasks.enabler_now: Rule checks on holder records and sanction list screening.
tasks.still_hard: Holders with complex ownership or treaty claims.
tasks.human_edge: Recognising a structure built to avoid withholding tax.
tasks.altitude: Less checking by hand; judgement on cases stays.

reach.learn: Whether flagged cases arrive better documented.

evidence.claim: Checks for completeness and fixed criteria are rules; judgement stays with a person.
No solely automated decision with legal effect without a legal basis.

assumptions: Boundary: verifying a dividend run; paying it is outside.
Input contract for s2: tax forms and residence recorded for holders by the registrar, about 85% complete; the rest are flagged; the sanction list from the official source; s2 is priced at that share.
Judging flagged cases keeps its full time.
unknowns: Share of holders with incomplete tax data.

already_counted.description: Brokerage clerk reviews rule flags that turn out fine.

incremental.description: Brokerage clerk updates rules when tax rates or treaties change.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many foreign holders with treaty claims; high: mostly domestic holders with complete data.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional
